summary: One persistent two-A800 temporal chain generated all ten windows with nine rolling source-camera-frame references, improving the worst raw overlap by 47.79% relative to the four-GPU two-chain profile while remaining 2.5460x faster and 60.723% cheaper in GPU-hours than baseline.
evidence: Verified generation time is 822.754838 seconds for 660 useful frames, or 0.802183 useful FPS and 29.9184x real time; measured cost is 0.457086 A800 GPU-hours.
All 660 source frames, ten immutable result hashes, one temporal chain, and nine previous-window camera-frame links are recorded.
Worst best-seam MAD is 7.4452 versus 14.2593 for the two-chain throughput profile; mean best-seam MAD is 4.7994 versus 5.2356.

The radius-4 stitch decodes all 660 frames and reports temporal consistency 0.96397, maximum transition ratio 6.0800, motion preservation 0.26370, and SHA-256 bf15763ff5ceeb26bd2a744045d76579bad2b758ffa787176e4e8693d5a5ff91.
lessons: A single rolling temporal dependency removes the independent-chain discontinuity, but camera-frame-only identity feedback accumulates late drift; speed-first parallelism and continuity-first dependency depth need separate operating profiles.
limitations: The stitched result remains review_required because its maximum transition ratio exceeds the prior accepted visual route and motion preservation is low.
Dense and all-seam contact sheets show no obvious source-human return, but no claim is made for exact action, flower/stem identity, contact physics, collision safety, or real-robot execution.
next_actions: Add a stateful cross-worker handoff or a bounded identity-refresh mechanism that limits rolling drift without reintroducing an independent-chain reset.
